Method of Attack: Phishing emails pretending to be from Attorney General's Office of Mexico City or Spanish Public Ministry
Email contains link redirecting to website dropping ZIP archive with loader module disguised as PDF
Loader fetches Delphi payload from remote HTTP file server
Loader gathers system info, installed AVs, cryptocurrency wallets, e-banking apps and sends to C2
Final payload signed with stolen ASUSTEK certificate and inflated by binary padding to evade sandbox
Use of CAPTCHA to evade analysis
Persistence via Registry keys to launch at system startup
Use of DGA (domain generation algorithm) for C2 communications
Backdoor capabilities: keylogging, auto-updation, web-injects, command execution, window manipulation, browser redirection, imitating mouse and keyboard
Impacted Systems: Employees of chemicals manufacturer in Spain
Workers of automotive and machinery makers in Mexico
Windows systems (implied by Registry keys and Windows-specific features)
Attack Vector: Remote HTTP file server delivering payload
